screens.prompt: In B4, join the first name in A2 and the last name in B2 with a single space between them.

hints.syntax: CONCAT takes the pieces one after another: =CONCAT(A2," ",B2).
hints.func-concat: CONCAT glues its arguments together in order, and the space between the names has to be one of the arguments.
hints.require-ref: Use the names in A2 and B2 rather than typing Ada and Lovelace, so the formula follows the row.
hints.value: That is not a first name, a space and a last name in that order. Check which cell comes first.
hints.error: Concatenated text divided by zero returns #VALUE!, because text cannot be a number.

docs.explain: The full name is three pieces in order: Ada, a space, and Lovelace. CONCAT takes them as arguments and glues them together, so =CONCAT(A2," ",B2) answers Ada Lovelace. The space is the piece people forget, because CONCAT(A2,B2) answers AdaLovelace, which looks like a name and is not one. The & operator does the same join and is shorter to type, so =A2&" "&B2 answers the same text. This drill is graded on CONCAT because that is the function it names. Either way the pieces come from cells, so changing the row changes the answer without touching the formula.

errors.text: The joined text was used where a number was expected, as when it is divided by a number.
The function name was typed wrongly, as when CONCAT is spelled CONCATE.

docs.atWork: Building a display name from two fields that a system stores separately, so the export reads as a name rather than as two columns.
docs.outcome: Glue cell values together and keep the spaces in the right places.

seo.title: CONCAT and & in Excel: join two cells
seo.description: Ada, a space, then Lovelace is the full name. CONCAT glues the pieces in order, the & operator joins them the same way, and the space is the part left out.
